key_insight: AlphaFISH combines spatial transcriptomics, spatial microbiome mapping, and AI to show that host-microbe interactions in colorectal tumors can predict aggressive disease and post-resection recurrence.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help identify colorectal cancer patients at higher risk of recurrence after surgery by reading spatial biology directly from biopsy tissue.
method: Sequencing-free spatial profiling at subcellular resolution
Integrates spatial gene expression with microbial microenvironment data
Transformer model learns joint embeddings from dual-omics and tissue architecture
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 149 biopsies from 68 patients, used a 4.27-million-cell reference atlas, and reported nearly 90% accuracy for pathology feature prediction and 81% accuracy for 1-year recurrence prediction in 28 followed patients.
watch_item: The recurrence result is based on a relatively small follow-up cohort, so broader validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Cohort-scale Spatial Host-Microbiome Predicts Post-Resection Recurrence in Colorectal Cancer
